slot.brief: Evaluate an indefinite integral of the form ∫ (polynomial)·(exponential or inverse-trig or log) dx requiring integration by parts, possibly applied twice.

stem: Evaluate the indefinite integral $\int x^2 e^x\,dx$.

verdicts.working: By parts twice: ∫x²eˣ dx = eˣ(x² − 2x + 2) + C; differentiating gives x²eˣ.

working:
$\int x^2e^x\,dx=x^2e^x-2\int xe^x\,dx$

Independent check: By parts twice: ∫x²eˣ dx = eˣ(x² − 2x + 2) + C; differentiating gives x²eˣ.
solution:
Using integration by parts twice,
$$\int x^2e^x\,dx=e^x(x^2-2x+2)+C.$$
